incoming.name: Phla-Pherá languages
incoming.excerpt: Alada, a lect that is sometimes included in the Phla-Pherá group, is spoken in southwestern Nigeria just southeast of Benin's administrative capital Porto-Novo.

outgoing.name: Capital
outgoing.excerpt: Porto-Novo (also known as Hogbonou and Adjacé (population 223,552 as of a 2002 census) is the official capital of the West African nation of Benin.

outgoing.name: Cotton
outgoing.excerpt: The region around Porto-Novo produces palm oil, cotton and kapok.

outgoing.name: Football
outgoing.excerpt: Stade Municipale and Stade Charles de Gaulle, or Charles de Gaulle Stadium, are the largest football stadiums in the city.

outgoing.name: Mosque
outgoing.excerpt: Other sites of interest include a Brazilian-style church, which is now a mosque, and the Institute of Higher Studies of Benin.

outgoing.name: Palm oil
outgoing.excerpt: The region around Porto-Novo produces palm oil, cotton and kapok.

outgoing.name: Petroleum
outgoing.excerpt: Petroleum was discovered off the coast of the city in the 1990s, and has become an important export.
